caseStudy.label: Luminate
caseStudy.heroTitle: Building Luminate: A Brand Identity for the Modern Storyteller
briefParagraphs: Luminate set out to redefine how independent creators present their work online. The client needed a brand identity and Kickstarter presence that felt premium, trustworthy, and instantly recognizable.
The team partnered with Waft Tech to design a full visual identity system and a campaign landing page that would help launch their MVP to a wider audience.
This case study walks through the discovery process, design decisions, and the results achieved during the engagement.
problemParagraphs: Luminate had a strong product but no cohesive brand language. Their existing visuals felt inconsistent across platforms, which made it hard for backers to trust the campaign.
The solution? A unified design system built from the ground up, anchored by a distinctive color palette and typography that could scale across web, social, and print.

solutions.heading: New Visual Identity:
solutions.text: We designed a complete brand system including logo, color palette, and typography that reflected Luminate's mission of empowering creators.

solutions.heading: Campaign Landing Page:
solutions.text: A conversion-focused landing page was built to support the Kickstarter launch, with clear storytelling and social proof sections.

solutions.heading: Asset Library:
solutions.text: We delivered a reusable component library so the in-house team could maintain consistency as the brand grew.

results.heading: Funding Goal Exceeded:
results.text: The Kickstarter campaign surpassed its $144,000 goal, driven in large part by the new brand presence.

results.heading: Stronger Brand Recognition:
results.text: Backers and press consistently cited the visual identity as a reason the campaign stood out.

caseStudy.thoughtsText: Luminate is a reminder that strong storytelling and strong design go hand in hand. We are excited to continue supporting their journey as they launch their MVP.

caseStudy.label: Lineage Journey
caseStudy.heroTitle: Lineage Journey: Making your spiritual journey better
briefParagraphs: Lineage Journey is an educational platform that helps users explore biblical history and heritage through interactive storytelling and multimedia content.
Waft Tech was brought on to design and build a website that could hold rich multimedia content, watch, read, listen, and shop, while remaining fast and easy to navigate.
problemParagraphs: The client had a large archive of video, audio, and written content but no unified place to house it. Visitors struggled to find related material, and the existing site felt dated and slow.

solutions.heading: Unified Content Hub:
solutions.text: We built a single platform combining watch, read, listen, and shop experiences under one cohesive design system.

solutions.heading: Related Content Engine:
solutions.text: A related-content module was added so visitors could naturally discover more relevant material as they browsed.

results.heading: Higher Engagement:
results.text: Average session duration increased significantly after launch as visitors explored more content per visit.

caseStudy.thoughtsText: Lineage Journey shows how thoughtful information architecture can turn a content archive into an engaging experience.

caseStudy.label: SUMMA
caseStudy.heroTitle: SUMMA: A smarter way to study and retain knowledge
briefParagraphs: SUMMA is a mobile learning app designed to help students retain knowledge through spaced repetition and bite-sized summaries.
We partnered with the founding team from the ground up, designing the brand identity and building the mobile application.
problemParagraphs: Students had access to plenty of study material, but no simple way to review it efficiently. Existing apps felt cluttered and were not built around proven learning science.

solutions.heading: Spaced Repetition Engine:
solutions.text: We built a review scheduling system based on spaced repetition to help users retain information long-term.

solutions.heading: Clean, Focused UI:
solutions.text: The interface was stripped down to essentials, keeping the user focused on one card at a time.

results.heading: Strong Early Adoption:
results.text: SUMMA saw strong week-one retention after launch, with users returning daily to complete review sessions.

caseStudy.thoughtsText: SUMMA proves that good learning design is as much about restraint as it is about features.

caseStudy.label: Chronotek
caseStudy.heroTitle: Chronotek: Designing a smarter way to track time
briefParagraphs: Chronotek is a time-tracking app built for freelancers and small teams who need a fast, frictionless way to log billable hours.
Waft Tech led the full UX design process and built the front end of the application.
problemParagraphs: Most time-tracking tools required too many steps to start and stop a timer, causing users to forget to log hours accurately, which directly affected their billing.

solutions.heading: One-Tap Timers:
solutions.text: We redesigned the core flow so starting and stopping a timer takes a single tap from any screen.

solutions.heading: Smart Reminders:
solutions.text: Gentle reminders nudge users to log time if a timer has been left running or forgotten.

results.heading: Fewer Missed Hours:
results.text: Users reported significantly fewer unbilled hours within the first month of using the redesigned app.

caseStudy.thoughtsText: Chronotek is a great example of how removing friction from a single core action can transform an entire product experience.

caseStudy.label: The Sharing Hope
caseStudy.heroTitle: The Sharing Hope: A website built to inspire generosity
briefParagraphs: The Sharing Hope is a nonprofit organization focused on community outreach. They needed a website that could clearly tell their story and make donating simple.
We designed and built a warm, accessible site that puts real stories and impact front and center.
problemParagraphs: The previous site buried the donate button several clicks deep, and it was not clear to visitors how their contributions made an impact.

solutions.heading: Impact-First Storytelling:
solutions.text: Real stories and outcomes were placed at the top of key pages to build trust before asking for a donation.

solutions.heading: Simplified Donation Flow:
solutions.text: The donate action is now accessible from every page in a single click.

results.heading: Increased Donations:
results.text: Online donations grew noticeably in the months following launch.

caseStudy.thoughtsText: Clear storytelling paired with a frictionless donation flow made all the difference for The Sharing Hope.

caseStudy.label: EcomStore
caseStudy.heroTitle: EcomStore: A storefront built to convert
briefParagraphs: EcomStore needed a modern, fast online storefront capable of handling seasonal traffic spikes without sacrificing checkout speed.
Waft Tech built a custom e-commerce platform tailored to their catalog and fulfillment process.
problemParagraphs: Their previous storefront was slow to load on mobile, and cart abandonment during checkout was unusually high.

solutions.heading: Performance Overhaul:
solutions.text: We rebuilt the storefront with optimized images and lazy loading, cutting mobile load times significantly.

solutions.heading: Streamlined Checkout:
solutions.text: Checkout was reduced from five steps to two, with guest checkout enabled by default.

results.heading: Lower Cart Abandonment:
results.text: Checkout completion rates improved meaningfully after the redesign.

caseStudy.thoughtsText: EcomStore is proof that speed and simplicity are two of the most powerful conversion levers in e-commerce.

caseStudy.label: DeskFlow
caseStudy.heroTitle: DeskFlow: Bringing order to the modern workday
briefParagraphs: DeskFlow is a desktop productivity app that helps teams organize tasks, notes, and files in one workspace.
We built the desktop application from the ground up, focused on speed and offline reliability.
problemParagraphs: The team was juggling multiple disconnected tools for tasks, notes, and files, leading to lost context and duplicated work.

solutions.heading: Unified Workspace:
solutions.text: Tasks, notes, and files now live in a single window with fast keyboard-driven navigation.

solutions.heading: Offline-First Architecture:
solutions.text: The app works fully offline and syncs automatically when a connection is restored.

results.heading: Faster Task Switching:
results.text: Early users reported spending noticeably less time switching between tools during their workday.

caseStudy.thoughtsText: DeskFlow shows that sometimes the biggest productivity win is simply reducing the number of tools someone has to open.

caseStudy.label: Guide
caseStudy.heroTitle: Guide: A travel companion built for spontaneous trips
briefParagraphs: Guide is a mobile app that helps travelers discover local spots and build itineraries on the fly, without heavy pre-planning.
Waft Tech designed the UX and built the mobile app end to end.
problemParagraphs: Existing travel apps required extensive upfront planning. The client wanted something that worked well for spontaneous, in-the-moment decisions.

solutions.heading: Location-Aware Suggestions:
solutions.text: The app surfaces nearby recommendations in real time based on the user's current location and time of day.

solutions.heading: One-Tap Itinerary Building:
solutions.text: Users can add any spot to their day plan with a single tap, no forms or manual entry required.

results.heading: High Daily Engagement:
results.text: Users opened the app multiple times per day while traveling, well above initial projections.

caseStudy.thoughtsText: Guide taught us that removing planning friction can be just as valuable as adding more features.
